Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

We will start with a new module today on nanomaterials.

Key details

  • The content will be nanomaterials, classification and deviation of properties from bulk material, and we will look at different properties of nanoparticles.
  • In today's class we will study of nanomaterials, about nanomaterials, the classification of nanoparticles, and the reasons for deviation in properties of nanomaterials from the bulk material.
  • The prefix nano is derived from the Greek word dwarf meaning very tiny.
  • One nanometer would be approximately equal when we have ten hydrogen atoms placed one next to the other or five silicon atoms.
  • aligned in a line.
  • Previous module we studied about molecular spectroscopy and we understood that when we study about molecules or atoms we need to use the quantum mechanical treatment.
  • But when the dimension becomes close to the nanometer, then we are going to observe.
  • Because the dimension are now, dimensions are closer to those of atoms or molecules.
  • because their properties are very different from that of the bulk materials.
  • All of us know that bulk gold as we see it is yellowish in colour.
  • That means there is some change in the optical property.
  • That means the activity has become so high something involved which is passive has become so active that it is combustible to the extent that it is used as a solid fuel in rocket propulsion.
  • Another property of importance is melting point of the materials when they are taken in the nanoparticle range becomes lower.
  • If we want to check purity of the material, we always quote the melting point.
  • This material will be classified as a nanomaterial.
  • And what would be nano science?
  • It is the study of the phenomena and synthesis, characterization, exploration, and exploitation of these nanostructure materials.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Let us first understand what we mean by a nanoparticle.
  • For example, gold.
  • In fact the a name golden colour has been given to gold.

Core explanation · 05:00–09:59

Before studying the reasons why nanomaterials behave so differently from the bulk material, let us talk about classification of nanomaterials based on their dimensions.

Key details

  • Now the first classification would be it will be called as a zero dimensional nanomaterial.
  • What does it mean?
  • Range exceeding 100 nanometers.
  • It's understood now that two of the dimensions are allowed to be outside of the nanorange.
  • films these will be classified as two dimensional nanomaterials only one dimension is now within the nano range but still we call it as a nanomaterial.
  • And then coming to three dimensional nanomaterials where all the three dimensions are outside of the nano range.
  • Then how is it a nanomaterial only specific types of materials where you have like say bundles of nanovires.
  • Nanomaterial, therefore, these overall will look like as if all the three dimensions are outside of the nanorange.
  • First and foremost reason which we should discuss here is that the large fraction of surface atoms per unit volume.
  • Atoms on the surface, but major of the atoms are in the bulk of the material.
  • But when we come to nanomaterials, what happens?
  • The particle size has.
  • Become so small now that on the surface you have a large number of surface atoms, whereas in the bulk we have very few atoms now.
  • Properties now are strictly governed by the surface atom because they are larger in number as compared to the bulk atoms.
  • When we have a platinum sheet as compared, which is we can say is bulk, whereas compared to platinum powder, but to a nanopowder.
  • Now the surface area, each particle now, the surface area has is more, and therefore overall surface area.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Example, as I said, nano clusters or quantum dots fall into this category of nanomaterials.
  • An example would be nanotubes and nanovires we can understand look at the picture here.
  • So such materials are also classified as three dimensional nanomaterials where we have all the three dimensions outside of the nanorange like for example dispersions of nanoparticles or we have bundles of nanovires.

Core explanation · 15:00–19:59

compared to nanomaterials where we'll have a maximum of ten to thousand atoms.

Key details

  • Now here, when we say one mole, that means we have 10 to the power 23 atoms, that means so many electrons, and also means that there are so many energy levels.
  • They'll be very close and almost continuous.
  • They will be continuous to the extent that in metals we know that the balance band and the conductance band are overlapping.
  • When we come to semiconductors, of course there is a small gap, nevertheless, these levels and the levels in the valence band and the condensed band, there are so many levels because there are so many atoms.
  • And these levels will be very close to one another that they will be continuous.
  • But when we come to nano range, what happens is now we have reduced the number of atoms.
  • There are fewer atoms, fewer electrons, so the density of states falls down.
  • And what we observe, say we are in a two dimensional.
  • quantum well then we'll find that the energy levels now because there are less number of atoms, less number of electrons, less number of energy stays.
  • And then when we come to zero dimensional nanomaterial the energy levels now are completely discrete and the energy gap has increased.
  • If you compare them with a molecule in a molecule we know we have absolutely discrete energy levels.
  • to the lumino, the highest occupied molecular orbital to the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital, and this is the energy gap.
  • But as these become more and more in number, if you go this way now.
  • When we come to bulk, we find that the valence band, there are so many.
  • Many energy levels now because of so many atoms there.
  • or the spatiment.
  • What do we understand?
  • That due to spatient or quantum confinement, the energy levels become more and more discrete and the energy gap increases.
  • This is the result of quantum confinement, and this is going to have a strong bearing on the properties, especially the electronic properties, electrical properties, and the optical properties.
  • And one more reason.
  • for the bulk material behaving differently from the nanomaterial, but the nanomaterial behaves different from the bulk, is that in the bulk material we find that there are lattice imperfections like wherever there are dislocations, kinks, etcetera, are found in the lattice.
  • Because the metal lattice is formed in such a way that layer after layer after layer is getting deposited of the metal.
  • And many times we do not get a perfect layer.
  • Rather there are some imperfections which are like dislocations or kinks are possible.
  • in the metal structure, it's a bulk metal structure.
  • But when you come to the nanomaterial range, what has happened now you just have to they're very small in size the particles.
  • Therefore very small lattice has to be formed and therefore there is less possibility of imperfections.
